item.title: Source code of the Estonian online voting system
item.description:
📝 IVXV online voting system The intention behind this repository is to make source code of the Estonian online voting system available for public review. The repository is not used for active development, but will be kept up to date, so the code that can be found here is the code that is used for election. As the voting system used for legally binding elections must strictly follow the legislation, the actual development of Estonian I-voting system and I-vote verification application is supervised by State Electoral Office of Estonia.
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/valimised/ivxv

item.title: Dam removals are bringing fish back across the northeastern United States
item.description:
📝 This can’t have surprised Thoreau, who knew that dams made for intractable opponents. Since 1912, more than 2,300 dams have been purged from waterways in the United States, most in the last quarter-century. After this and other dams were removed from the Elwha River in Washington State, long-absent salmonids came surging back.
🔗 Read more: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/dam-removals-are-bringing-fish-back-across-the-northeastern-united-states-striking-down-one-tiny-barrier-at-a-time-180989679/

item.title: Pele – Mermaid diagrams as themeable SVG
item.description:
📝 Pele is a lightweight open source library that renders Mermaid diagrams to SVG, themed with CSS variables. Write Mermaid syntax, Pele renders it to SVG. pele {2 --pele-bg: #fffcf0;3 --pele-fg: #100f0f;4 --pele-muted: #6f6e69;5 --pele-line: #100f0f;6 --pele-surface: #f2f0e5;7 --pele-surface-alt: #e6e4d9;8 --pele-border: #cecdc3;9}PeleThemesVariablesLightDarkPeleMermaid.
🔗 Read more: https://pele.run/

item.title: Microsoft and CMU Team Up to Train Early Career Software Engineers
item.description:
📝 He's in Seattle, working at his full-time job as a software engineer at Microsoft and taking classes through the Preceptorship for AI-accelerated Software Engineering (PRAISE) program, which CMU and Microsoft launched to train early career software engineers for the rapidly changing computer science landscape. At Microsoft, selected early career engineers, or preceptees, work with senior engineering preceptors to build AI-accelerated software engineering skills through structured guidance, mentorship and application to their day-to-day Microsoft work. These classes train students on how to incorporate machine learning into the software they write and to use AI tools while developing that software.
🔗 Read more: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/news/2026/microsoft-cmu-praise
